key_insight: A transfer-learning plus hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász loss upgrade to BiSeNetV2 substantially improves reflective seam segmentation without adding model complexity.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a lightweight, real-time perception boost for autonomous welding robots operating on shiny, hard-to-segment construction surfaces.
method: Start from BiSeNetV2 and apply transfer learning for seam segmentation.
Use a hybrid Cross-Entropy–Lovász optimization to improve boundary and overlap quality.
Target reflection-robust learning rather than increasing network size or runtime cost.
evidence_signal: The proposed method reached 81.76% Joint IoU and 90.73% mIoU, improving Joint IoU by 22.36 points over the OHEM baseline while keeping FLOPs, parameters, and inference speed unchanged.
watch_item: Performance gains are shown in a specific welding dataset and may require careful validation when deployed on new geometries, lighting setups, or camera conditions.
paper_title: Enhanced Seam Segmentation for Automated Welding Robot in Construction Through Transfer Learning: Addressing Limitations of Bilateral Segmentation Network
